item.title: TNGC-SIDM I: Evolution of massive cluster mergers under the self-interacting dark matter paradigm
item.description: arXiv:2610.18957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Merging galaxy clusters provide an ideal laboratory for testing the self-interacting nature of dark matter. In this paper, we present a pilot study of magnetohydrodynamical cosmological zoom-in simulations of two cluster mergers selected from TNG-Cluster, with $M_{\rm 200c} \sim 9\times10^{14}~M_\odot$ and $M_{\rm 200c}\sim 2\times10^{14}~M_\odot$. The simulations are performed with both standard collisionless cold dark matter (CDM) and self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), assuming an isotropic, velocity-independent cross-section of $\sigma_{\rm T}/m_\chi = 1~\rm cm^2~g^{-1}$, with an additional $0.5~\rm cm^2~g^{-1}$ run for the low-mass system, and the mass resolution and galaxy formation model are unchanged from TNG-Cluster. We show how dark matter self-interactions produce an isothermal core in the dark matter halo, generate unique substructures in the intracluster light, and introduce variation in the multi-wavelength observables of the intracluster plasma. Using these simulations, we test the validity of observational probes for dark matter self-interactions in cluster mergers. We find that the shock-to-shock separation shows similar evolution in the self-interaction models tested here, providing a reference for distinguishing the $\sim100-200~\rm kpc$-scale difference in halo separation induced by self-interactions. Moreover, the dark matter halo centroid of the main cluster in the massive cluster merger is offset from the brightest cluster galaxy by as much as $\sim20~\rm kpc$, larger than the offset in the sub-cluster. This offset persists beyond 4 Gyr after the first pericenter passage. Our results indicate that sample selection plays a key role in testing the possible self-interacting nature of dark matter using cluster mergers, and that double radio relic cluster mergers and massive clusters with evidence of an ancient major merger offer a promising testbed for this purpose.
item.dc:creator: Wonki Lee, Dylan Nelson, Myungkook J. Jee, Giulia Despali, Mark Vogelsberger, Annalisa Pillepich, Cian Roche, Kyle Finner, Hyungjin Joo, Daisuke Nagai, John ZuHone

item.title: Audible curvaton: modulated phase transition as the origin of large-scale curvature perturbations and gravitational wave anisotropies
item.description: arXiv:2610.18975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a post-inflationary first-order phase transition modulated by a light spectator field as the origin of primordial large-scale curvature perturbations. Spectator fluctuations acquired during inflation modulate the bubble nucleation history, generating curvature perturbations together with correlated intrinsic gravitational-wave (GW) anisotropies. We show that this mechanism can reproduce the observed amplitude of curvature perturbations while producing a loud stochastic GW background in the frequency bands of space-based detectors such as LISA, Taiji, and TianQin. A concrete benchmark yields strongly enhanced intrinsic GW anisotropies and a local primordial non-Gaussianity signal within reach of future large-scale-structure surveys.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Yuan Ai, Gabriele Franciolini, Xin Wang, Xiang-Xi Zeng

item.title: Forecasting a Cosmological 21 cm Stacking Detection with Early HIRAX Data
item.description: arXiv:2610.18981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-reionization 21 cm intensity mapping provides a powerful technique for efficiently mapping the Universe on large scales. The Hydrogen Intensity and Real-time Analysis eXperiment (HIRAX) is a compact and highly redundant radio interferometer designed to exploit this technique. We present a forward modelling pipeline for forecasting a statistical detection of the cosmological 21 cm signal with HIRAX through cross-correlation with an external source catalogue. We simulate the cosmological signal using the halo model and propagate it, together with Galactic and extragalactic foreground emission and instrumental noise, through a model of an early-stage 36-dish HIRAX array configuration. We generate simulated visibilities, apply delay-domain foreground filtering, and construct cross-correlation-ready ringmaps for an observing time of 120 days with a single zenith pointing over the frequency range from 700 to 800 MHz, covering approximately 3547 deg$^2$ of the sky. We investigate the prospects for an early statistical signal detection by stacking these ringmaps at the known three-dimensional positions of sources from an overlapping external survey. Specifically, we quantify how delay-domain foreground filtering, the number of stacking sources, catalogue completeness, and source redshift uncertainties affect the detection significance. We find that redshift precision is the most critical requirement: while spectroscopic redshifts with $\sigma_z / (1+z) \sim 0.001$ preserve a significant stacking signal even under realistic foreground filtering and substantial catalogue incompleteness, photometric redshift uncertainties of $\sigma_z / (1+z) \sim 0.01$ strongly suppress the signal for realistic delay cutoffs. Applying the framework to a Euclid-like spectroscopic galaxy sample, we recover a minimum signal-to-noise ratio of 11 for our most conservative delay cutoff of 100 ns.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Hitz, Devin Crichton, Alexandre Refregier

item.title: Scalar-Assisted Growth of Supermassive Black Holes: Boson-Mass Windows and Observational Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2610.18986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a phenomenological cosmological model of black-hole growth in which a finite baryonic reservoir and a bosonic scalar cloud feed the black hole simultaneously. The baryonic component accretes through an Eddington-like channel, while the scalar cloud transfers mass through an effective quasibound-state decay rate. Evolving the system directly in redshift within a flat $\Lambda$CDM background, we scan over $\mu$, $M_0$, $M_{c,0}$, and $M_{b,0}$ to assess whether scalar-assisted accretion can accelerate the formation of $10^9M_\odot$ supermassive black holes. We find that the scalar contribution is highly selective in parameter space. For the mass scales explored here, scalar transfer is most efficient for $\mu\sim10^{-19}-10^{-16} \mathrm{eV}$, producing rapid cloud depletion and significantly earlier black-hole growth, while outside this interval the evolution remains mainly baryonic. More generally, this efficient window reflects a preferred range of the dimensionless coupling $\alpha=\mu M_{\rm BH}$ and therefore shifts approximately as $\mu\propto M_{\rm BH}^{-1}$. Comparison with observed quasar masses and luminosities instead favors lower boson masses, broadly around $\mu\sim10^{-21}-10^{-20}\mathrm{eV}$. These results are not necessarily in tension, since the boson mass that maximizes early growth depends on the characteristic black-hole mass and evolutionary stage. This separation between dynamical efficiency and observational compatibility leaves open complementary roles for different bosonic mass scales in supermassive black hole growth and dark-matter phenomenology.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Castelo Mourelle, Dar\'io N\'u\~nez Z\'u\~niga, Saeed Fakhry, Nicolas Sanchis-Gual

item.title: Kinetic Theory of the EFTofLSS : A Halo-Based Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.19001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure (EFTofLSS) provides a coarse-grained description of the non-linear gravitational clustering of dark matter, in which the effects of short-scale physics are encoded in an effective stress tensor and a set of counterterms. In this work, we develop a framework to investigate the physical origin of these counterterms by relating the effective stress tensor to the dynamics of individual dark matter halos in cosmological N-body simulations. We find that halo accretion contributes to the trace of the halo-based effective stress tensor, contributing to the background pressure and effective sound speed, while anisotropic accretion generates the traceless part, consequently contributing to the shear viscosity. For the halo population with $M_\mathrm{vir}>10^{12}\,M_\odot/h$, we find that halos account for $\sim\!95\%$, $\sim\!85\%$, and $\sim\!70\%$ of the full box background pressure, effective sound speed, and shear viscosity, respectively, depending on the EFT cutoff scale. The contributions to the counterterms are dominated by cluster-scale halos, $M_\mathrm{vir} \sim 10^{14} - 10^{15}\,M_\odot/h$ and halos with larger inflow rates, supporting an interpretation in terms of accretion-driven, out-of-equilibrium dynamics. Our results provide a short-scale, kinetic-theory interpretation of the EFTofLSS counterterms and establish a framework for connecting the properties and dynamics of short-scale structures to physics-informed priors for large-scale cosmological observables.
item.dc:creator: Om Kishor Hebbar, Caio B. de S. Nascimento, Arka Banerjee

item.title: The Atacama Cosmology Telescope: DR6 Constraints on Isotropic Time-Dependent Cosmic Birefringence from Axion-like Particles
item.description: arXiv:2610.19049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) with sufficiently low masses are dark matter candidates because they could account for much or all of the observed dark matter energy density and help explain observations of galactic substructure. Such pseudoscalar fields could couple to photons, causing a time-dependent rotation of the polarization of the light with an oscillation frequency equal to the ALP mass. We use measurements of the polarization of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) by the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) between 2017 and 2022 to search for this effect using an EB power spectrum estimator. By probing oscillation periods from days to years, the data constrain the coupling between ALPs and photons for ALP masses between $2.5\times 10^{-23}$ eV and $4.8\times 10^{-20}$ eV. We find no evidence for such a signal and set a 95% upper bound on the axion-photon coupling constant, $g_{\phi\gamma} < 1.1\times10^{-11}\left({m_\phi}/{10^{-21}\,\mathrm{eV}}\right)\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1} .$ This limit assumes that ALPs make up all of the dark matter and that the ALP field amplitude is stochastically distributed, which leads to more conservative bounds than the deterministic-field assumption used in some previous CMB polarization analyses. Among searches for ALP-photon coupling using CMB polarization, we set the strongest bounds to date under the stochastic-field assumption. This work develops a methodology to analyze over 10,000 time-sliced "depth-1" polarization maps from ACT, a data product that will be standard for time-domain astrophysics with the Simons Observatory, enabling searches with a higher sensitivity and observing span.
item.dc:creator: Zachary B. Huber, Huajian Yang, Steve K. Choi, Erminia Calabrese, Vera Gluscevic, Sigurd Naess, Michael D. Niemack, Lyman A. Page, Alexander van Engelen, Edward J. Wollack

item.title: Cosmology with strong gravitational lenses
item.description: arXiv:2610.19598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Three of the most pressing open questions in cosmology -- the nature of dark energy and dark matter, and the growing tension in the value of the Hubble constant H$_0$ -- call for cosmological probes that are independent of, and complementary to, traditional methods. Strong gravitational lensing offers exactly that: a purely gravitational probe of the universe's expansion history and matter distribution, sensitive to dark matter's presence regardless of whether it interacts with light. Time-delay lenses and multiplane lenses can measure H$_0$ and the dark energy equation of state directly, while the distortion of lensed images can reveal the abundance and internal structure of dark matter subhalos. After a brief theoretical and historical introduction, I review recent breakthroughs enabled by JWST and by advances in lens modeling and stellar dynamics. Examples include the recent measurement of H$_0$ with 3\% precision in flat $\Lambda$ cold dark matter cosmology, and a tentative detection of dark matter self-interaction. Strong lensing is entering a pivotal era: wide-field surveys with Euclid, Rubin, and Roman, and radio surveys with the Square Kilometer Array, are poised to increase the number of known strong lenses by orders of magnitude, positioning strong lensing to play a central role in answering these open questions in the decade ahead.
item.dc:creator: Tommaso Treu (UCLA)

item.title: specwizard: A Public Python Framework for Creating Synthetic Absorption Spectra from Hydrodynamical Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.19862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present specwizard, a publicly available modular Python package for generating synthetic absorption spectra from hydrodynamical simulations. The code combines atomic data from the National Institute of Standards and Technology database with ionisation fractions computed using the cloudy spectral synthesis code for multiple ionising backgrounds, enabling consistent modelling of bound--bound and bound--free absorption for resonant transitions of all ions. specwizard employs a column-density--conserving projection scheme, includes natural line broadening for the Lyman series, and offers optional treatments of instrumental resolution and noise for direct comparison with high-resolution quasar spectra. As example applications of the code, we shoot sightlines through the eagle cosmological simulation to generate a z = 3.2 synthetic quasar spectrum containing H i Lyman-series transitions, including damping wings and Lyman-limit absorption. Additionally, we compute metal-absorption lines probing the circumgalactic medium of simulated galaxies, and investigate the correlated absorption of H i and Si iii. We demonstrate that specwizard applied to outputs from eagle accurately reproduces key observational diagnostics of the Lyman-alpha forest, including the redshift evolution of the mean transmission, the transmission PDF and the transmission power spectrum. We take advantage of the fact that the eagle simulation also reproduces the measured evolution of the temperature-density relation to infer the evolution of the amplitude of the ionizing background, finding excellent agreement with recent theoretical models and measurements.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'es Ar\'amburo-Garc\'ia, Tom Theuns, Joop Schaye, Alexey Boyarsky

item.title: Low-cost neural summaries for cosmological inference: an ensemble of convolutional neural networks trained on approximate simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.19891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning can build near-optimal summary statistics for extracting cosmological information from the large-scale structure of the Universe. Training them, however, requires large numbers of costly simulations. We aim to build a neural summary trained on fast, approximate low-resolution simulations that remains informative when applied to higher-resolution ones, reducing the cost of the training set. We train an ensemble of convolutional neural networks with different architectures to compress the matter overdensity fields of low-resolution particle-mesh simulations. The outputs of a subset of networks are concatenated into a summary statistic, which we use to constrain $\Omega_{\rm m}$ and $\sigma_8$ from high-resolution particle-mesh simulations, each about a thousand times more costly than their low-resolution counterparts. Theoretical predictions are provided by a Gaussian process emulator built from the high-resolution simulations. We test three strategies for selecting the smallest informative subset of networks. Constraints are compared with those from a reference power spectrum analysis. We also consider dark matter halo catalogues from independent high-resolution $N$-body simulations. The neural summary extracts information beyond the binned power spectrum. Using multiple networks is essential: a single network can be less informative than the power spectrum. A greedy search based on posterior volume provides the tightest constraints with the fewest networks. The neural summary also outperforms the power spectrum for dark matter haloes, at different number densities and redshifts, despite being trained on low-resolution matter fields at $z=0$. This work demonstrates that an ensemble of networks trained on approximate simulations yields a summary statistic that remains informative on higher-fidelity data, including dark matter haloes. (Abridged)
item.dc:creator: I\~nigo S\'aez-Casares, Davide Bianchi, Matteo Calabrese, Luigi Guzzo

item.title: Testing Departures from the $\Lambda$CDM model in f(T) Gravity with DESI DR2
item.description: arXiv:2610.20002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent analyses combining DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements with other cosmological observations have reported indications of departures from the $\Lambda$CDM model within dynamical dark energy scenarios. We investigate whether such deviations are reproduced consistently in $f(T)$ gravity and whether they persist when different cosmological observations are combined. Using the DESI DR2 BAO measurements, Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB), and Pantheon+ Type Ia Supernovae (SNe Ia) sample, we constrain three representative $f(T)$ models: the power-law, exponential, and hyperbolic-tangent models. We compare the constraints obtained from different combinations of data, distinguishing changes in marginalized parameter distributions from changes in the relative statistical performance of the models. For the power-law model, the mild deviation from the $\Lambda$CDM model obtained from BAO+CMB disappears after the SNe Ia data are included. In contrast, the exponential model retains a preference for a nonzero deformation parameter in the full analysis, while the allowed parameter space of the hyperbolic-tangent model changes substantially after the CMB distance priors are included. Importantly, the parameter-level deviation found for the exponential model does not lead to a clear statistical preference over the $\Lambda$CDM model according to the information criteria, whereas the hyperbolic-tangent model shows a poorer statistical performance for the combined data. Despite these differences in the model constraints, the inferred transition redshift $z_T$ remains relatively stable among the three models and data combinations. Our results show that the departures from the $\Lambda$CDM model indicated by DESI analyses are not a generic feature of $f(T)$ gravity, but depend strongly on the specific modified gravity parameterization and on the combination of cosmological observations.
item.dc:creator: Jie Zheng, Mingzhi Wang, Ming Zhang

item.title: Galaxy-to-galaxy stochasticity has a limited impact on reionization and the 21-cm signal at fixed mean emissivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.20184v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Galaxy-to-galaxy stochasticity may be less important for reionization, IGM heating, and the 21-cm signal than commonly assumed. We find that most of its apparent impact arises because introducing or removing scatter changes the mean emissivity of the galaxy population, rather than from redistributing radiation at fixed mean emissivity. We use the Meraxes semi-analytic model to separate these effects. For ionising sources, we vary the scatter in the escape fraction and in the SFR-halo mass relation across three source prescriptions. For the X-ray heating sources, we introduce luminosity scatter and also separately remove SFR scatter. Without recalibration, these modifications shift the mean emissivities, changing the timing of reionization and IGM heating and producing substantial differences in the 21-cm signal. Once the relevant mean emissivities are restored, however, the global ionizing and thermal histories converge and the power-spectrum differences fall below the forecast sensitivity of a deep SKA-Low observation. There are some weak changes in ionisation morphology, depending on which galaxies dominate the ionising emissivity and on their response to photoheating. Within the models and scales considered here, calibrating the mean radiative emissivities is therefore substantially more important than resolving their galaxy-to-galaxy scatter.
item.dc:creator: Shihai Zhu, Yuxiang Qin

item.title: Exact map-space beam convolution via spin-mapmaking
item.description: arXiv:2610.20231v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Forthcoming cosmic microwave background (CMB) experiments are targeting ambitious science goals, including the exploration of the particle content of the Universe across cosmic times and the search for the faint signal from primordial gravitational waves. To pursue these goals, CMB experiments will house an unprecedented high number of detectors that will dramatically enhance their sensitivity. This will in turn require a tight control of instrumental systematics, demanding efficient and precise simulation of systematic effects. Leveraging spin-mapmaking, we present a map-based method to propagate beam convolution systematics to the map-level, especially well-suited for main-beam studies. From the scanning strategy information compressed into precomputed h-maps and the beam and sky harmonic coefficients, our method directly outputs beam convolved maps. We validate against pixel-centered TOD-level 4{\pi} convolution for circular, elliptical, and Planck HFI scanning beams, demonstrating that our method retains agreement to numerical precision, while operating in map space. This formalism enables efficient simulation of beam convolution systematics across the full focal plane of upcoming experiments. As a first practical application, we demonstrate the ability to efficiently produce beam-convolved simulated Planck maps, showing excellent agreement with the QuickPol pipeline at the power-spectrum level. We release a public code, Smarties4Planck, to easily generate such maps for broader use.
item.dc:creator: Camille Demay, Magdy Morshed, Martina Gerbino, Luca Pagano

item.title: Thermalization of the Primordial Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background
item.description: arXiv:2610.20325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is conventionally believed that the Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background (SGWB) from inflation provides information about the earliest universe. However, in this Letter, we present a different picture. Our analysis starts from the observation that the inflation-predicted spectrum implies gravitons reside in high-occupation states, which significantly enhances their self-interactions and triggers rapid thermalization. We show that approximately $80\%$ of the primordial gravitons participate in this thermalization, forming a Bose--Einstein distribution and thereby erasing the primordial information. Evaluated using typical inflation parameters, this thermalized spectrum yields a present-day peak frequency of $f_{0, \text{peak}}^{(\text{th})} \sim 1.4 \times 10^8 \, \mathrm{Hz}$ in the hundred-megahertz band with a peak amplitude of $\Omega_{0, \text{peak}}^{(\text{th})} \sim 3.5 \times 10^{-13}$. Due to the sharp drop-off away from the peak, the resulting spectrum lies beyond the reach of low-frequency observatories like PTAs, LISA, and LIGO, but remains uniquely accessible to high-frequency detectors such as microwave cavity resonators and dielectric haloscopes.
item.dc:creator: Hongguang Zhang, Zhengyang Qiu, Sirui Wang, Jiayi Wei

item.title: Bouncing Bianchi Type I Universes with Interacting Vacuum
item.description: arXiv:2610.20357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the global dynamics and cosmological viability of non-singular solutions in an anisotropic Bianchi type I universe featuring an interacting vacuum energy component $V$ and a perfect fluid $\rho$, extending previous work based on a Robertson-Walker geometry. By modeling the energy-momentum transfer via a phenomenological four-vector $Q_\mu$, we reduce the field equations to a four-dimensional autonomous dynamical system for the expansion rate $\Theta$, total shear $\sigma$, energy density $\rho$, and vacuum component $V$. We examine two distinct forms for how the interaction depends on $\rho$ and $V$: a linear coupling $Q_1 \propto \Theta[\xi(V_\Lambda - V) + \chi \rho]$ and a non-linear coupling $Q_2 \propto \Theta \rho (1 - V/V_\Lambda)$. Using a potential-energy analogy and phase-space analysis, we show that the linear model $Q_1$ naturally admits non-singular bouncing trajectories. In contrast, unlike the Robertson-Walker case, for the non-linear interaction $Q_2$, invariant boundary surfaces in phase space strictly constrain the domain of expansion ruling out cosmological bounce scenarios for physical matter configurations.
item.dc:creator: Marco Bruni, Rodrigo Maier, Thomas Waters

item.title: Origin of the red spectral tilt in Inflation without an Inflaton
item.description: arXiv:2610.20378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), a de Sitter (dS) background drives inflation, and the graviton bilinear generates scalar perturbations at second order, with no inflaton or additional fundamental scalar field. We investigate how this scenario can account for the observed scalar spectral tilt. The tensor-mode dependence of the scalar power spectrum gives the consistency relation $n_s-1=2n_T$, since it contains four tensor mode functions. The scalar spectral tilt $n_s\simeq0.9649$ at CMB scales therefore gives $n_T\simeq-0.0175$, independent of the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, hence different from the standard single-field slow-roll prediction $n_T=-r/8$. A full time-dependent calculation of $\phi_2$ in exact dS leads to an almost scale-invariant scalar power spectrum, with a small blue infrared residual on the order of $n_s-1\simeq+4\times10^{-4}$. In order to account for the observed red tilt, we introduce a slow drift in the Hubble rate, parametrized by $\varepsilon=-\dot H/H^2$. The tensor tilt is then given by $n_T=-2\varepsilon$, implying $n_s-1\simeq-4\varepsilon$, at leading order. The observed tilt requires $\varepsilon_\ast\simeq0.0088$, far exceeding the drift that can be sustained by the classical graviton backreaction, for which we find $|\varepsilon_{\rm self}|\lesssim10^{-11}$. Therefore, we investigate the quantum break-time of dS as the origin of the background evolution. In this picture, the scalar tilt becomes $n_s-1=-4C_qN_{sp}(H/m_{pl})^2$, where $C_q$ is an order-one depletion coefficient, and the tilt is directly connected to the particle content of dS, $N_{sp}$. The evolution of the drift itself further predicts a positive running of $\alpha_s=+\tfrac12(1-n_s)^2\simeq+6\times10^{-4}$. These results conclude the distinctive observational predictions of the IWI scenario, establishing it as a falsifiable alternative to standard inflaton-driven models.
item.dc:creator: Raul Jimenez, Daniele Bertacca, Mariam Abdelaziz, Sabino Matarrese, Angelo Ricciardone, Marisol Traforetti

item.title: Joint Line Intensity Recovery from Multi-Tracer Cross-Correlations
item.description: arXiv:2610.20467v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Line intensity mapping (LIM) provides a unique window into the high-redshift universe, but the separation of signals from overlapping emission lines and bright continuum foregrounds remains a central analysis challenge. At millimeter wavelengths in particular, [CII], [CI] and numerous CO transitions overlap with comparable brightness, leading to significant spectral confusion. This work presents a joint likelihood framework that incorporates multi-tracer cross-correlations both between distinct LIM tracers and with external galaxy surveys. By jointly fitting all auto- and cross-spectra between the LIM and galaxy data, this approach combines the spatial and spectral information in each dataset to break degeneracies between overlapping lines and recover individual bias-weighted line intensities at fixed cosmology, even at redshifts where no direct cross-correlation is available. We validate this framework on realistic mocks of an extended SPT-SLIM-like survey spanning 125-175 GHz over 100 deg$^2$, combined with an LSST Y1-like photometric galaxy catalog, and recover CO(2-1) through CO(6-5) and [CI](1-0) over $0.3\lesssim z\lesssim4$ in the presence of bright continuum foregrounds. We demonstrate that adding the photometric galaxy data tightens line constraints by a factor of $\sim$3-4 where the galaxies overlap the lines in redshift, and by $\sim$20-50\% at higher redshifts beyond the galaxy coverage, where the gain comes indirectly from constraining the low-redshift interlopers. These results highlight external tracer overlap as a primary consideration when optimizing the frequency coverage and footprint of near-future LIM experiments.
item.dc:creator: Carlos E. Sierra, Kirit S. Karkare

item.title: Identity Crisis: Untangling Mass-Ordering Artifacts from Compact-Object Pairing in Gravitational-Wave Populations
item.description: arXiv:2610.18962v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mass distributions of binary black hole mergers inferred from gravitational-wave observations offer clues to how binaries form. These distributions conventionally label the heavier component as the primary, with mass $m_1$, and the lighter as the secondary, with mass $m_2$, such that $m_1 \geq m_2$. This ordering folds the physically labeled mass distribution along the equal-mass line, potentially reshaping the underlying population structure. In this Letter, we determine which population features can arise from mass ordering and which require genuine astrophysical structure. We show that ordering alone can produce (1) an $m_2$ distribution that declines more rapidly than the $m_1$ distribution, without intrinsic differences between the physically labeled components, and (2) an apparent concentration along equal masses, without correlations that preferentially pair black holes of equal mass. Moreover, different physically labeled populations can produce the same ordered mass distribution. Crucially, however, a preferred companion mass that remains constant as $m_1$ increases requires a characteristic mass scale already present in the physically labeled population. Applied to binary black hole mergers in the fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog, our model recovers such a scale near $m_2 \simeq 50\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. Around this scale, the merger-rate density declines much more rapidly toward higher $m_2$ than toward lower $m_2$, ruling out an equal or weaker high-$m_2$ decline at 99.45% credibility. This structure therefore requires a characteristic mass scale in at least one physically labeled component, but masses alone cannot determine which component carries it. Any formation model reproducing the observed high-mass binary black hole merger population must contain such a scale.
item.dc:creator: Soumendra Kishore Roy, Asad Hussain, L. A. C. van Son, Maya Fishbach, Carl L. Rodriguez, Will M. Farr

item.title: The Dance of the Little Red Dots: Spectroscopy of Two Blue Companions at z = 3.9 and 5.5 Reveals Young, Metal-Poor Starbursts Merging with Their LRDs within a Few Hundred Myr
item.description: arXiv:2610.18968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact, red sources, abundant at $4 \lesssim z \lesssim 9$ and likely powered by massive black holes. Photometric studies have found blue companions around them, but none has yet been confirmed spectroscopically. This Letter presents the only two LRD-companion pairs with spectroscopy of both members in the literature: "Waltz" at $z = 3.9$ and "Tango" at $z = 5.5$, with projected separations of $3.6$ and $2.5$ kpc. Both companions lie at the redshift of their LRD, within $132 \, \rm km \, s^{-1}$ and $57 \, \rm km \, s^{-1}$, and are physically identical, but $524$ Myr apart: starbursts $\lesssim 50$ Myr old, metal-poor ($0.2 \, \rm Z_\odot$), dust-free, dynamically cold, and as bright as the LRDs themselves in the rest-frame UV. The LRD in Waltz hosts a $\approx 3 \times 10^{6} \, \rm M_\odot$ black hole accreting at half the Eddington rate, a factor of a few above the birth mass of a direct collapse black hole, and is embedded in gas as metal-poor as its companion. Orbital modeling shows that Tango is bound in $81\%$ of the allowed orbits and that Waltz is bound if its host halo exceeds $5 \times 10^{10} \, \rm M_\odot$. Both blue companions then merge with their respective LRD within a few hundred Myr. We conclude that we are observing what heavy seeding requires: a young black hole beside the metal-poor starburst that the synchronized-pair scenario predicts, in the last steps of a cosmic dance that ends in a merger, and in a galaxy seeded by its black hole.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Pacucci, Pierluigi Rinaldi

item.title: jax-SNANA: A GPU-accelerated Supernova Framework for the SBI Era
item.description: arXiv:2610.19000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present jax-SNANA, a JAX reimplementation of the supernova analysis framework SNANA. jax-SNANA enables GPU-accelerated transient simulations and light curve fitting, supernova standardisation and cosmological inference. Running in single precision on an NVIDIA A100 GPU, jax-SNANA simulates more than 100,000 LSST-observed supernovae per second and fits 5,000 light curves per second after JIT compilation, a two orders-of-magnitude increase over current tools, essential for analysing samples at the scale expected from LSST. jax-SNANA currently supports the SALT and BayeSN spectral energy distribution (SED) models as well as physical models from redback-jax and a variety of SN SED templates; light curve fitting is supported with both photometric and spectroscopic redshifts. We fully validate the accuracy of jax-SNANA by comparing to SNANA, finding excellent consistency between the two across a variety of tasks. The code provides a modular JAX end-to-end supernova cosmology pipeline, user-extensible to support new features including different SED templates and photometric classification algorithms. jax-SNANA has been designed with future applications of simulation-based inference in mind, providing fast simulations and enabling fully compiled on-the-fly simulations to be generated within the training loop of downstream SBI tasks. jax-SNANA extends beyond SNANA by supporting simulations of generic SN-host galaxy relationships and multiple sub-populations of events, for example originating from young and old progenitors. jax-SNANA is publicly available at https://github.com/mattgrayling/jax-snana and installable through pip.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Grayling

item.title: The connection between massive galaxies and their dark matter haloes from $z=0.25$ to $z \sim 4$ from the combined COSMOS, XMM-LSS and ECDF-S fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.19030v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding how galaxies populate and grow within dark matter haloes is essential for linking the observed evolution of galaxies to the hierarchical growth of structure. We present a galaxy clustering analysis using optical and near-infrared data from the UltraVISTA and VIDEO surveys covering $9.3$ deg$^2$ across the COSMOS, XMM-LSS and ECDF-S fields, $\sim 5\times$ larger than previous comparable studies, providing sufficient volume to determine the halo occupation of the most massive galaxies to $z\sim 4$. We measure the angular two-point correlation function for stellar-mass-selected galaxies over $0.25<z<4$ and by combining the three fields, we reduce the cosmic variance by a factor of $\sim2$ compared to the individual fields. The stellar-to-halo mass ratio peaks at a halo mass of $M_{h}\approx10^{12} {\rm M}_{\odot}$ and is a maximum at $z\sim 1$. For the most massive galaxies, the peak halo mass ($M_{h}^{\rm peak}$) increases from $z=1\rightarrow 0$, while the peak stellar mass in such haloes remains approximately constant, indicating that at $z<1$ massive galaxy formation becomes less efficient. We also find a steady increase in the satellite fraction since $z\sim 1$, from which we infer that massive halos continue to grow hierarchically while their central galaxies experience suppressed stellar-mass growth. We suggest this is due to the central massive galaxies having their growth controlled by feedback from active galactic nuclei feedback, likely from low-power stochastic radio emission.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Stylianou, Matt J. Jarvis, Rohan G. Varadaraj, Peter W. Hatfield, Joel Hamlett, Catherine L. Hale, Tariq Yasin

item.title: The Contribution of Mergers and Accretion to Dark Matter Halo Assembly: An Excursion Set Theory Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.19312v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the relative contributions of mergers and accretion to the assembly of dark matter haloes within the framework of Excursion Set Theory (EST). We extend a variance-discretized merger-tree algorithm, which recursively reconstructs all branches of a complete merger tree and introduces a merger-ratio criterion for distinguishing mergers from accretion. The method is validated by comparing the resulting progenitor distributions with the analytical conditional first up-crossing distribution, showing excellent agreement over a wide range of halo masses and redshifts. We find that the accretion contribution depends strongly on the adopted merger-ratio threshold. For large merger ratios ($MR=0.1$--$0.25$), accretion accounts for up to $\sim70\%$ of the mass growth of massive haloes, whereas including all resolved mergers ($MR=10^{-6}$) reduces the accretion contribution to $\sim40\%$. These values are in good agreement with previous N-body simulation results. The accreted mass exhibits a nearly self-similar distribution in the mass-redshift plane, with the dominant contribution arising from progenitors in the range $10^{-3}M_0 \lesssim M \lesssim 10^{-1}M_0$ and predominantly at $0.5 \lesssim z \lesssim 2$. Our results demonstrate that EST-based merger trees provide an accurate and computationally efficient framework for investigating halo assembly and quantifying the relative roles of mergers and accretion in hierarchical structure formation.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Kameli

item.title: Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.19440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.
item.dc:creator: Tanmay Vachaspati, Anja Wachowitz

item.title: All Quiet on the Vector Front: Scalar Growth and Perturbative Control in Horndeski--Weyl-squared Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.20156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Higher-order curvature corrections to general relativity arise naturally in many fundamental theories and provide phenomenologically interesting low-energy effective field theories. However, higher-derivative terms can introduce ghost modes, which call the validity of such models into question. Here, we thoroughly investigate the classical linear stability of the most general second-order scalar-tensor theory, namely the Horndeski theory of gravity, augmented by a Weyl-squared term in the action. We consider shift-symmetric de Sitter and power-law FLRW backgrounds and study the evolution of linear perturbations. Vector perturbations are free of gradient and tachyonic instabilities for a positive Weyl-induced mass squared. Tensor perturbations necessarily contain a ghost; their superhorizon branches are bounded, while a frozen-background calculation identifies a separate finite-momentum stability condition. The scalar sector instead contains a growing long-wavelength branch for all expanding backgrounds we consider, which is inherited by at least one of the gauge-invariant Bardeen potentials. We show that this growth enters the Bardeen potentials through an inverse-gradient factor $a^2/k^2$: the dynamical scalar fields remain bounded on the inflationary backgrounds, the direct contribution of the growing shear to the clock-matched tidal field cancels, and the electric part of the Weyl tensor decays. We discuss the implications of our results for perturbative control and for the phenomenological viability of theories including quadratic curvature corrections.
item.dc:creator: Antonio De Felice, Guillem Dom\`enech, Jan Tr\"ankle

item.title: Correlation between gravitational wave frequencies as a signature of new black hole physics
item.description: arXiv:2610.20167v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We point out that for black holes (BH) of the same mass, despite of arising from two entirely different physical arguments, the peak frequency of the coarse-grained gravitational wave (GW) spectrum of gravitons $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}$ is very close to the peak frequency of the GW spectrum produced from binary BH mergers $f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}$. In particular, we find that $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}/f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}\approx 2.3$ independent from BH mass or population. If BHs are still evaporating, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{-1}$ with $M_i$ is the initial BH mass. If BHs evaporated in the radiation (matter) dominated era, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{1/2}$ ($\propto M_i$) respectively after taking into account redshift effect. Any deviation from the aforementioned magical ratio would indicate new BH physics. The sweetest frequency ballpark to look for this correlation is around $10^{14}\ \rm Hz-10^{20}\ \rm Hz$ where both GW spectra are allowed to have maximum amplitude. As a demonstration of what the new physics could be, we consider a phenomenological self-similar regular BH model of Hayward featuring a single hair parameter. The observed ratio of peak frequencies can be used to directly infer the hair parameter, along with crucial properties of the novel BH solution such as Hawking temperature, horizon size, and innermost stable circular orbit. We also comment on the pros and cons of correlating frequencies among other GW sources such as formation, population fluctuation, and sudden transition of adiabatic perturbation.
item.dc:creator: Ngo Phuc Duc Loc

item.title: A Step-Like Transition Underlying the Life and Death of Galaxies
item.description: arXiv:2610.20505v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How galaxies stop forming stars is a complex and central problem in astrophysics. Numerous physical mechanisms have been proposed, yet a simple, unified framework connecting these mechanisms remains lacking. Here, we derive a step-function quenching response from the fundamental principle of gas mass conservation, governed by the competition between gas-supply and gas-depletion timescales. This response also enables the gas-supply timescale to be inferred from the observed quenched fraction. Applying this method to approximately 350,000 galaxies, we find a characteristic gas-supply timescale of ~1 Gyr, reveal distinct inside-out and outside-in quenching signatures associated with supermassive black holes and dark matter halos, respectively, and identify galaxies with intermediate stellar surface mass densities as occupying a critical state for quenching and rejuvenation. Our work establishes a unified physical framework in which a simple step-function response captures how diverse physical processes regulate galaxy quenching and the resumption of star formation through their effects on the competition between gas-supply and gas-depletion timescales.
item.dc:creator: Zhicheng He, Enci Wang, Luis C. Ho, Yingjie Peng, Huiyuan Wang, Yong Shi, Tao Wang, Yongquan Xue, Tinggui Wang

item.title: Can bosenovae deplete the galactic dark matter?
item.description: arXiv:2610.20507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: No: neither through the bosenovae of gravitational atoms formed around stars and compact objects, nor through those of boson stars formed in the galactic dark-matter halo. We assume that all the dark matter consists of ultralight bosons with attractive self-interactions, which can be captured in the gravitational potential of astrophysical objects or condense into self-gravitating configurations. When these systems collapse in a bosenova, part of their mass is turned into relativistic radiation that escapes the galaxy. We bound the mass that a single object can eject and sum it over realistic models of the Milky Way and of other types of galaxies. For gravitational atoms, with realistic stellar populations and stellar evolution, the stars of the Milky Way deplete at most $\epsilon^{\rm GA}_\star\simeq3\times10^{-9}$ of its halo, and the pump is equally negligible in other galaxies. The central black hole, Sgr A$^*$, could reach $\epsilon^{\rm GA}\sim10^{-3}$, but only for a boson mass disfavoured by ultrafaint dwarf galaxies and beyond the validity of the perturbative treatment, where only a geometric bound on the dark matter flux is available. For boson stars feeding on the rest of the halo, these would radiate at most $\sim3\times10^{-5}$ of the Milky-Way halo and $0.1\%$ of a DF2-like one.
item.dc:creator: Samuel G\'omez G\'omez, Joshua Eby

item.title: Binary-lens amplification of starlight: from magnification flares to quasi-periodic tracking of orbital evolution
item.description: arXiv:2610.20557v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHB) are expected at the center of galaxies as a result of galaxy mergers. The dynamics and evolution of SMBHBs shed light on the evolution and formation of galaxies, the gravitational wave background and the nature of gravity. Many methods have been proposed to identify sub-parsec SMBHBs via the detection of gravitational waves or the modulation of the emission from the surrounding gaseous environment. In a previous study, we proposed a new method of identifying SMBHBs in non-active galactic nuclei via gravitational lensing. The caustics, i.e. the source positions with a divergent magnification, exhibit a complex extended geometry which rotates with the binary period. Each caustic-crossing produces an extreme magnification by up to a factor of $10^{6}$. In this work, we generalize the previous study and describe the rich phenomenology of binary-lens amplification of starlight (BLAST). We explore the electromagnetic transients produced when accounting for the relative proper motion of the source, either a single or a binary star, the eccentricity and precession of the SMBHB, and the relative inclination. Systems where a star rapidly drifts across the caustic produce a single- or double-peaked flare. In the opposite limit, a star with no relative proper motion produces quasi-periodic lensed starlight (QPLS), i.e., repeated peaks that track the system's orbital evolution. We determine the expected magnification and peak duration in different circumstances, and calculate the magnification curves and their Fourier transforms. This study may help construct search pipelines to identify SMBHBs in electromagnetic time-domain surveys.
item.dc:creator: Hanxi Wang, Bence Kocsis, Miguel Zumalac\'arregui

item.title: Dark Energy Survey Year 6 Results: improved mitigation of spatially varying observational systematics with masking for the MagLim++ lens sample
item.description: arXiv:2509.07943v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: As photometric surveys reach unprecedented statistical precision, systematic uncertainties increasingly dominate large-scale structure probes relying on galaxy number density. Defining the final survey footprint is critical, as it excludes regions affected by artefacts or suboptimal observing conditions. For galaxy clustering, spatially varying observational systematics, such as seeing, are a leading source of bias. Template maps of contaminants are used to derive spatially dependent corrections, but extreme values may fall outside the applicability range of mitigation methods, compromising correction reliability. The complexity and accuracy of systematics modelling depend on footprint conservativeness, with aggressive masking enabling simpler, robust mitigation. We present a unified approach to define the DES Y6 JOINT footprint, integrating observational systematics templates and artefact indicators that degrade mitigation performance. This removes extreme values from an initial SEED footprint, leading to the final JOINT footprint. By evaluating the DES Y6 lens sample MagLim++ on this footprint, we enhance the Iterative Systematics Decontamination (ISD) method, detecting non-linear systematic contamination and improving correction accuracy. While the mask's impact on clustering is less significant than systematics decontamination, it remains non-negligible, comparable to statistical uncertainties in certain w(theta) scales and redshift bins. Supporting coherent analyses of galaxy clustering and cosmic shear, the final footprint spans 4,031.04 deg2, setting the basis for DES Y6 1x2pt, 2x2pt, and 3x2pt analyses. This work highlights how targeted masking strategies optimise the balance between statistical power and systematic control in Stage-III and -IV surveys.

item.title: Evidence of galaxy cluster rotation and intrahalo gas motions in the cosmic microwave background
item.description: arXiv:2512.10951v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report the first robust evidence for the rotational kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (rkSZ) effect: the dipolar signal produced by the Thomson scattering of cosmic microwave background (CMB) photons off intracluster gas in dynamically active systems (including rotations and mergers). By combining CMB intensity and polarization measurements from the \emph{Planck} satellite with spectroscopic member-galaxy redshifts from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey in a sample of 25 X-ray cross-matched, low-redshift ($0.02< z< 0.09)$, massive ($10^{13.9}\lesssim M_{\rm 500c}/M_\odot \lesssim 10^{14.6}$) galaxy clusters, we detect a dipolar rkSZ signature aligned with the estimated angular momentum of each cluster, ruling out a chance fluctuation at 99.98\% confidence (3.6$\sigma$). The significance of this measurement is enhanced by several new methodological improvements for isolating the rkSZ signal from primary CMB fluctuations and noise. The amplitude and shape of the signal are qualitatively consistent with predictions from state-of-the-art hydrodynamical simulations. These results establish a new tool with which to probe the dynamical state of galaxy clusters using CMB data.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Goldstein, J. Colin Hill

item.title: Probing scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves in the nHz band: NANOGrav and SKA
item.description: arXiv:2604.13012v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) have recently attracted considerable interest, both as a possible explanation for the nanohertz signal reported by the Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) collaboration and for their connection with primordial black hole (PBH) physics. In addition to SIGWs, scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves (STGWs) have emerged as a promising cosmological source of the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB). In this paper, we compute the STGWs generated during a generic matter-dominated (MD) era, as well as during an early matter-dominated (eMD) epoch followed by a sudden transition to the standard radiation-dominated (RD) stage, working in the Poisson gauge. We find that, in a purely MD age, the corresponding energy density rapidly dilutes, whereas in the presence of an eMD phase it remains non-vanishing due to the short duration of the eMD period. We then investigate whether the STGW signal could provide a dominant contribution to the \texttt{NANOGrav 15-year} dataset and we forecast the prospects for its detection with future observations by the Square Kilometre Array (SKA). In particular, we consider STGWs generated during both eMD and RD eras, including their linear-order contributions. We further inject the scalar-induced contribution, both as an additional component and as the only signal, and compare the spectra against the same datasets. Our results show that, although the SIGWs still appear to provide the dominant contribution and the posteriors are tightly constrained by the requirement of avoiding PBH overproduction, the GWs induced by scalar-tensor mixing constitute a viable target for future, more sensitive nano-Hz detectors of the SGWB.
item.dc:creator: William Iania, Angelo Ricciardone

item.title: Cosmo-PINN: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Cosmological Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2605.30139v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce Cosmo-PINN, a Physics-Informed Neural Network for reconstruction of the cosmological theory. In this work we demonstrate the application of the Cosmo-PINN in the reconstruction of the dark energy equation of state parameter $w_{DE}\left( z\right) $ directly from late-time cosmological observations. This framework overcomes the main limitation shared by Gaussian Process and Artificial Neural Network reconstruction approaches, where the recovered solution is driven by the data and it is not necessarily true that it is physically consistent, by embedding the cosmological constraints directly into the loss function as constraints, ensuring that the reconstructed quantities satisfy the physical laws at every point during the training. For the training of the network, we employed background data, and specifically the Baryon Acoustic Oscillation from DESI DR2, the Cosmic Chronometers and three different Supernova compilations, while we simultaneously introduce the cosmological parameters $% H_{0},~\Omega _{m0}$ and $r_{\mathrm{drag}}$ as trained parameters. The reconstruction shows that the trained $w_{DE}\left( z\right) $ crosses the phantom divide around $z=0.5$ in agreement with the value obtained by the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder model. In the quintessence scenario, the dark energy equation of state parameter is forced to the $\Lambda $CDM limit in the past, that is $w_{DE}\left( z\right) \rightarrow -1 $. Finally, we demonstrate the significance of imposing the physical constraints within the loss function by comparing the Cosmo-PINN reconstruction against a purely data-driven neural network with the same architecture.
item.dc:creator: Andronikos Paliathanasis

item.title: Time-reversed stochastic inflation in the quantum well
item.description: arXiv:2605.31323v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Time-reversed stochastic inflation solves the stochastic evolution of the inflationary universe backward in time, by counting the number of e-folds from the end of quantum diffusion towards some initial state. The point of view of observers attached to the end-of-inflation hypersurface is thus enforced. In this work, we exactly solve time-reversed stochastic inflation in a flat and bounded potential, the so-called quantum well. At given lifetime, the field behaviour is found to be either indistinguishable from the one obtained in a semi-infinite flat potential, or, subject to enhanced stochasticity where any memory of the initial state is erased. The derived distribution of curvature perturbations reduces to the semi-infinite result for small fluctuations while it develops exponential tails for the large ones. Such tails arise for both positive and negative values, and decay twice as fast as the one obtained in the standard forward stochastic inflation. These differences may have important consequences for tail-sensitive phenomena, such as primordial black hole formation.
item.dc:creator: Chiara Animali, Baptiste Blachier, Nanoka Okada, Christophe Ringeval, Tomo Takahashi, Koki Tokeshi

item.title: Field-Level Baryon Acoustic Oscillation Reconstruction of the DESI DR1 Luminous Red Galaxies with Linear Field Transformer (LiFT)
item.description: arXiv:2609.14862v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the first application of neural field-level baryon-acoustic oscillation (BAO) reconstruction to real spectroscopic survey data. We develop Linear Field Transformer (LiFT), a 3D vision transformer that takes as input the observed galaxy field, its standard reconstruction, and a set of context channels encoding local line of sight, survey coverage, and redshift, and learns to correct standard reconstruction toward the linear density field. We construct a forward-modeling pipeline to produce mock lightcones similar to the DESI Data Release 1 (DR1) luminous red galaxy (LRG) sample, and train LiFT on these. We validate LiFT on held-out simulations, as well as on additional mocks which differ in gravity solver, halo finder, HOD, cosmology, and fiber-assignment history, as well as on mocks analyzed with a distorted distance-redshift relation; ultimately, we find unbiased dilation parameters with consistently tighter constraints than standard reconstruction. Applied to the DESI DR1 LRGs, LiFT improves errors on $\alpha_{\rm iso}$ by 13%, 24%, and 30% and on $\alpha_{\rm AP}$ by 5%, 22%, and 30% relative to the DESI DR1 standard reconstruction analysis in the LRG1, LRG2, and LRG3 bins respectively; meanwhile, our DR1 central values remain consistent with DR1 and DR2. This equates to a factor of 1.2, 1.7 and 2.0 increase in Figure of Merit (or effective survey volume) if one were to only use standard reconstruction. Ultimately, these results establish LiFT as a validated, survey-ready tool for current and upcoming galaxy surveys.
item.dc:creator: Liam Parker, Uro\v{s} Seljak, Adrian E. Bayer, Richard Feder, David Valcin

item.title: Evolving dark energy and a younger Universe from cosmic inhomogeneity
item.description: arXiv:2609.31543v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Joint analyses of baryon acoustic oscillations, type Ia supernovae and the cosmic microwave background show a preference for an evolving dark-energy equation of state, and recent studies suggest that cosmic inhomogeneities can produce an apparent evolution of dark energy within general relativity. Here we examine this effect within a framework in which the possibility that matter can be unevenly distributed enters the expansion dynamics directly. The framework yields redshift-dependent effective values of the Hubble constant and of the dark-energy density parameter without introducing a new free parameter. Using CMB-inferred parameters to fix the homogeneous limit, we find that the dark-energy density parameter increases by about eight percent toward the present, from 0.679 to 0.735, while the inferred Hubble constant shifts from the Planck value toward the range obtained from local measurements. Both trends are broadly consistent with published estimates from supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, X-ray clusters and gravitational waves, although a joint analysis of the underlying data is left for future work. Integrating the resulting expansion history gives a present-day cosmic age of 13.521 Gyr, compared with 13.827 Gyr for the homogeneous model; we interpret the difference of 0.306 Gyr as a global time dilation between the two descriptions. The framework also yields the homogeneous-limit dark-energy density parameter, two thirds, from the formation of volume alone. The predicted redshift dependences can be tested against forthcoming measurements of cosmic distances and expansion rates.
item.dc:creator: Jacky David Yang, Hans-Otto Carmesin

item.title: How much can shape degeneracies affect the Hubble constant measurement?
item.description: arXiv:2610.15999v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Cluster lens models are constrained almost entirely by observed lensed image positions, leaving a large space of mass perturbations with arbitrary amplitudes such that they reproduce every image exactly. Such degeneracies are known as shape degeneracies (ShaDes). We show that these ShaDes shift the observed time delays, by the difference of the perturbing potential between the two images, without depending on the number of source/lens planes. Bounding their amplitude by preserving the positivity of the convergence, image multiplicity, and parity, in MACS J0138.0$-$2155, they can contribute at least $\simeq7$ days to the delay between the detected images of SN-Encore (i.e., $17.5\%$ of the measured value of $39.8$ days) and $\simeq112$ days (i.e., $2.8$--$3.7\%$ of predicted value of $3,000-4000$ days) to the reappearance intervals predicted for SN-Encore and SN-Requiem. These error bars transfer one-to-one to $H_0$, and remain invisible in comparisons of independent models.
item.dc:creator: Ashish K. Meena, Prasenjit Saha, Liliya L. R. Williams, Derek Perera

item.title: A Very Rich Bimodal Galaxy Cluster Merger: RXC J0032.1+1808
item.description: arXiv:2512.14945v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The galaxy cluster RXC J0032.1+1808 has been well-studied with optical imaging and gravitational lensing mass maps, both of which reveal an elongated morphology in the north-south direction. We find that its X-ray morphology is bimodal, suggesting that it is in the process of merging; combined with a previously reported detection of a radio relic, we suggest that the system is seen after first pericenter. We extract the global X-ray temperature and unabsorbed luminosity from archival XMM-Newton data, finding $T_X=8.5^{+1.1}_{-0.9}$ keV and $L_X=1.04 \pm 0.03 \times 10^{45}$ erg s$^{-1}$ at 90% confidence in the 0.5-10 keV energy range. We conduct a redshift survey of member galaxies and find that the line-of-sight relative velocity between the two subclusters is 1002-1785 km/s at 68% confidence, although the BCGs have an even larger difference of 2466 km/s. We use publicly available hydrodynamic simulations to show that it cannot be a head-on merger; it is consistent with an impact parameter of 0.5 or 1 Mpc. We also use the simulation set to find initial constraints on the time since pericenter (${\approx}$315-550 Myr) and the locus of possible lines of sight.
item.dc:creator: David Wittman (UC Davis), Rodrigo Stancioli (UC Davis), Christopher Hopp (UC Davis), Faik Bouhrik (UC Davis), Reinout van Weeren (Leiden Observatory), Andrea Botteon (INAF-IRA)

item.title: CHRONOS Science Program
item.description: arXiv:2603.10070v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cryogenic sub-Hz cROss torsion-bar detector with quantum NOn-demolition Speed meter (CHRONOS) is a proposed cryogenic torsion-bar interferometer for precision measurements in the 0.1-10 Hz band. A Sagnac speed-meter readout, power and signal recycling, and balanced homodyne detection provide control of the optical response and quantum measurement correlations. This White Paper describes the science program, detector design, calibration, and staged experimental development. The reference sensitivity uses a multi-input quantum model, including rear-mirror vacuum fields and measurement-back-action correlations, combined with classical noise. Two operating points are optimized for complementary power-law-integrated sensitivity objectives. Gravitational-wave forecasts use this common noise budget and state their source and observing assumptions. The program includes intermediate-mass black-hole binaries, stochastic backgrounds, quantum measurement, and terrestrial gravity perturbations. Dark-matter applications are discussed as response and feasibility studies. A differential gravitational calibrator provides a proposed Yukawa-gravity test whose systematic floor is improved by subtracting auxiliary harmonics. These are conditional projections: experimental reach requires validation of the noise, transfer functions, environmental backgrounds, and systematic uncertainties described here.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Inoue (on behalf of CHRONOS collaboration), Masashi Hazumi (on behalf of CHRONOS collaboration), Hsiang-Yu Huang (on behalf of CHRONOS collaboration), Vivek Kumar (on behalf of CHRONOS collaboration), Ippei Obata (on behalf of CHRONOS collaboration), Mario Juvenal S Onglao III (on behalf of CHRONOS collaboration), Daiki Tanabe (on behalf of CHRONOS collaboration), Ta-Chun Yu (on behalf of CHRONOS collaboration)

item.title: Collider Probes of Dark Energy Microphysics
item.description: arXiv:2606.27441v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The physical origin of dark energy remains one of the most profound open questions in modern physics. Although cosmological observations tightly constrain the equation of state parameter $w$, this information alone does not reveal the underlying microphysics, as many distinct theoretical models can reproduce the same expansion history. A key discriminator among these models is the sound speed of dark energy perturbations, yet this quantity remains largely unconstrained by current astrophysical observations. In this work, we propose a fundamentally new approach: using collider measurements of beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) mediator resonances as a probe of dark energy microphysics. We construct a unified effective-field-theory framework in which a dynamical dark energy scalar is coupled, through symmetry-motivated derivative interactions, to a pseudoscalar mediator in the 2HDM+$a$ model. These interactions naturally induce invisible decays and modify the propagation of the BSM mediator in a dark energy background, leading to measurable distortions of resonance properties at colliders such as the LHC. We show that the decay widths, branching ratios, and kinematic structure of the mediator resonance become sensitive to the propagation properties of dark energy fluctuations, in particular the sound speed. As a result, collider observables provide a direct and complementary handle on dark energy microphysics, with the potential to distinguish between models that are otherwise indistinguishable through cosmology alone. Our results establish a new paradigm in which high-energy collider experiments can probe the physics of cosmic acceleration, revealing a connection between the smallest and largest scales in nature and opening a novel experimental pathway to uncover the fundamental origin of dark energy.
item.dc:creator: Chaitanya Bashyam, Alfredo Gurrola, Andres Florez, Cristian Rodriguez

item.title: Investigation and Mitigation of a Prominent Off-Axis Stray Light Path in Rubin Observatory Commissioning
item.description: arXiv:2606.31939v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The "scratched tape" stray light feature is the most prominent and prevalent stray light artifact identified during the commissioning of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The scratched tape feature originates when light from large off-axis angles (~20 deg) passes between the mid-level and center-section light baffles, reflects off the primary mirror, and illuminates the LSST Camera focal plane. This scenario represented an unobstructed stray light path to the sky during Rubin commissioning due to delays in the integration of the dome slit light-wind screen. This document describes the identification, modeling, characterization, and mitigation of the scratched tape stray light artifact.
item.dc:creator: Alex Drlica-Wagner, Alessio Taranto, Gabriele Rodeghiero, Joshua E. Meyers, John Andrew, Douglas R. Neill, Christian Aguilar, Brian Stalder, Robert H. Lupton, Aashay Pai, Lee S. Kelvin, Aaron E. Watkins, Luca Rosignoli, Hannah M. M. Pollek, Anastasia Alexov

item.title: Axion Misalignment Across First-Order Phase Transitions
item.description: arXiv:2607.01333v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When the axion mass is generated during a first-order phase transition and becomes non-vanishing only inside expanding true-vacuum bubbles, the standard picture of misalignment production is qualitatively modified. Using lattice simulations in an expanding universe, we study dark matter production within such a framework and identify two distinct regimes. For rapid transitions, the onset of oscillations is delayed until bubble percolation, enhancing the relic abundance. For slower transitions, spatial gradients generated by expanding bubbles suppress the effective misalignment angle through the bubble misalignment mechanism. We derive a semi-analytical expression for the relic density that provides a unified description of both regimes and accurately reproduces the simulation results. Finally, we show how this mechanism also modifies isocurvature perturbations and the small-scale matter power spectrum, with important implications for axion minicluster formation.

item.title: Quantum Field Theory Of Cosmological Perturbations Induced By Ultralight Dark Matter
item.description: arXiv:2607.27133v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The growth of primordial perturbations during the matter-dominated era is primarily driven by dark matter. Ultralight scalar fields (ULDM) are a promising candidate for this role, conventionally modeled as operating in a classical, high-occupation regime. In this work, we develop a first-principles field-theoretic framework to investigate the impact of ULDM on linear cosmological perturbations during matter domination, explicitly retaining its quantum nature. Deriving a closed equation for the graviton field dynamics, we compute and regularize its source terms for a generic Gaussian initial state of the ULDM field within the adiabatic (WKB) approximation, employing the middle-point working assumption for non-local terms. After gauge-fixing we find that, contrary to previous claims, the classical condensate of ULDM has no influence on gravitational wave propagation. However, the time-dependent graviton effective mass induced by quantum pressure of the squeezed state can drive parametric resonance in specific primordial gravitational wave modes. We demonstrate this growth is negligible for non-relativistic ULDM at matter-radiation equality under the assumption of a power-law squeezing spectrum for masses in the range $m \sim 10^{-21}{-}10^{-24}$ eV.
